question: Does training on 63 rivers instead of 12 give better forecasts for the same 12 rivers, and for rivers never seen?
outcome: Given training on 63 rivers instead of 12, median NSE 1 day ahead for the same 12 rivers goes from 0.59 to 0.61 (onsets warned 19% to 16%); for rivers never seen, from 0.22 to 0.39 with basin properties (0.31 to 0.44 without them; 50 training rivers instead of 11); the verdict is NOT YET.
outcome_caveat: With the river gauge, 1 day ahead (lowest to highest single training in brackets): median NSE 0.590 (0.542 to 0.598) with the 12 rivers in training, 0.609 (0.581 to 0.603) with 63: no clear difference for NSE (every single seed above every single seed of the reference: no; higher in 10 of 12 rivers, p = 0.007). Onsets warned 18.7% (18.0% to 18.5%) -> 16.2% (11.9% to 17.2%) at the fixed high-flow level: hits 114 -> 99, false alarms 164 -> 101, CSI 0.147 -> 0.139; 11 onsets only the 63-river model warns of and 26 only the 12-river model: exact McNemar p = 0.020; the seed rule flags a clear loss in the share of onsets warned (every single seed of the 63-river model below every single seed of the 12-river model); the paired onsets differ (fewer onsets warned and fewer false alarms; CSI 0.147 -> 0.139); at the warning level chosen on the validation years (a multiple of the high-flow level: 0.90 against 1.00) 132 onsets (21.6%) against 114 (18.7%), false alarms 195 against 164, CSI 0.164 against 0.147; on all high-flow days at the fixed level CSI 0.508 against 0.480 (better) and false share 27% against 32%. Without the gauge: NSE 0.443 (0.355 to 0.434) against 0.458 (0.411 to 0.477): no clear difference for NSE (every single seed above every single seed of the reference: no; higher in 8 of 12 rivers, p = 0.042); onsets warned 17.2% (16.2% to 19.5%) -> 18.5% (17.0% to 20.0%) at the fixed high-flow level: hits 105 -> 113, false alarms 496 -> 440, CSI 0.095 -> 0.108; 20 onsets only the 63-river model warns of and 12 only the 12-river model: exact McNemar p = 0.215; the seed rule finds no clear difference and the paired onsets do not differ. At 2 days ahead with the gauge: onsets warned 8.3% (7.7% to 9.1%) -> 6.8% (5.9% to 8.6%) at the fixed high-flow level: hits 79 -> 65, false alarms 112 -> 57, CSI 0.074 -> 0.064; 3 onsets only the 63-river model warns of and 17 only the 12-river model: exact McNemar p = 0.003; the seed rule finds no clear difference, but the paired onsets do differ (fewer onsets warned and fewer false alarms; CSI 0.074 -> 0.064); at 3 days ahead: onsets warned 6.1% (5.5% to 7.3%) -> 5.8% (4.3% to 6.9%) at the fixed high-flow level: hits 68 -> 65, false alarms 89 -> 56, CSI 0.056 -> 0.055; 5 onsets only the 63-river model warns of and 8 only the 12-river model: exact McNemar p = 0.581; the seed rule finds no clear difference and the paired onsets do not differ. The 63-river models ran 1700 updates on average against 1233 for the 12-river controls (best at 1100 against 633), that is 559 against 1689 training sequences per river at the best update: at equal updates each river gets about a fifth of the training. Five times the update limit and the patience window (lstm63eq_wq: up to 10000 updates, a check every 500, stop after 6 checks without gain): it ran 4100 updates on average, but its kept networks are at 1500, 1000, 1000, 1000 and 1000 updates (mean 1100; 559 training sequences per river against 1689 for the 12-river control), where those of lstm63_wq are (mean 1100); the validation score of the 63 rivers peaks there and falls afterwards (seed 0: 0.372 at 1500 updates, 0.326 at the last check (4500); seed 1: 0.377 at 1000 updates, 0.319 at the last check (4000); seed 2: 0.378 at 1000 updates, 0.346 at the last check (4000); seed 3: 0.378 at 1000 updates, 0.286 at the last check (4000); seed 4: 0.377 at 1000 updates, 0.339 at the last check (4000)), so a longer patience window did not move the optimum, and this arm did not test equal training per river (that needs about 3300 updates, fixed rather than early-stopped). Its scores: NSE 0.617 (0.585 to 0.603); against the 12-river control no clear difference for NSE (every single seed above every single seed of the reference: no; higher in 11 of 12 rivers, p = 0.021); onsets warned 18.7% (18.0% to 18.5%) -> 16.5% (11.9% to 19.5%) at the fixed high-flow level: hits 114 -> 101, false alarms 164 -> 114, CSI 0.147 -> 0.139; 11 onsets only the five-times-limit model warns of and 24 only the 12-river model: exact McNemar p = 0.041; the seed rule finds no clear difference, but the paired onsets do differ (fewer onsets warned and fewer false alarms; CSI 0.147 -> 0.139); against lstm63_wq no clear difference for NSE (every single seed above every single seed of the reference: no; higher in 6 of 12 rivers, p = 0.569); onsets warned 16.2% (11.9% to 17.2%) -> 16.5% (11.9% to 19.5%) at the fixed high-flow level: hits 99 -> 101, false alarms 101 -> 114, CSI 0.139 -> 0.139; 7 onsets only the five-times-limit model warns of and 5 only lstm63_wq: exact McNemar p = 0.774; the seed rule finds no clear difference and the paired onsets do not differ. Rivers never seen (weather only), 1 day ahead, median NSE: with basin properties 0.216 with 11 training rivers (05_lobo.py: one training per river) and 0.387 with 50 (five-seed average; single trainings 0.343, 0.377, 0.359, 0.328, 0.374), without properties 0.313 and 0.439 (single trainings 0.428, 0.408, 0.432, 0.411, 0.430). Against the 05 numbers the seed rule reads clear gain with properties (p = 0.007; every 50-river seed above the single 05 training: yes) and clear gain without (p < 0.001; every 50-river seed above the single 05 training: yes); but each single 50-river training is +0.127, +0.161, +0.144, +0.112, +0.158 above the 05 number with properties (higher in 10, 10, 8, 11, 9 of 12 rivers; Wilcoxon p = 0.052, 0.092, 0.077, 0.027, 0.034) and +0.116, +0.095, +0.119, +0.099, +0.117 without (p = 0.001, 0.034, 0.001, 0.002, 0.001). Averaging five seeds adds 0.017 to 0.031 NSE to a single 50-river training, and the 05 numbers are single trainings. For scale, the same rivers when in training score 0.443 with the 12-river model (a seed average; its seed 0, the in-training partner of 05_lobo.py, scores 0.434, the best of its three seeds), 0.383 without properties (one training) and 0.458 with the 63-river model. Onsets of the never-seen rivers: at the model's own level (the rule of 05_lobo.py for a river without a gauge) 23.4% -> 21.9% with properties and 18.5% -> 21.1% without; at the observed level, which such a river does not have, with properties: onsets warned 20.5% -> 15.7% (15.7% to 16.9%) at the fixed high-flow level: hits 125 -> 96, false alarms 899 -> 509, CSI 0.083 -> 0.086; 21 onsets only the 50-river model warns of and 50 only the 11-river model: exact McNemar p < 0.001; the seed rule flags a clear loss in the share of onsets warned (every single seed of the 50-river model below every single seed of the 11-river model); the paired onsets differ (fewer onsets warned and fewer false alarms; CSI 0.083 -> 0.086). The number of training rivers, their variety and their nearness to the 12 all differ between the two designs and were not separated by it: the nearest training gauge is a median of 39 km away with the 50 against 110 km with the 11, the nearest training basin in property space 1.42 against 2.23. The gain over the 05 models does not rank with the distance to the nearest of the 50 training gauges (Spearman rho -0.18, p = 0.572 with properties; -0.31, p = 0.331 without; 12 rivers), and the 5 rivers whose nearest training gauge is no closer with the 50 gained a median of +0.149 and +0.096 (all 12: +0.132 and +0.081); the independent review (round 1, on the networks of seeds 0-2 and their three-seed averages) also scored the saved 50-river networks on the 12 and on 15 further never-seen rivers whose flow record has gaps (n = 27) and found that their NSE does not fall with the distance to the nearest training gauge (Spearman rho +0.09, p = 0.669 with properties; +0.24, p = 0.238 without; results/review_more_basins.json); a buffered leave-out or a dose-response over random subsets of the 50 would separate scale from nearness (not done). One model scores all 12 rivers, so its seed noise is shared by all of them.

lstm63_wq.label: one LSTM trained on 63 rivers (the 12 and 51 others), past weather + river gauge + basin properties, scored on the 12 only

lstm63_w.label: one LSTM trained on 63 rivers (the 12 and 51 others), past weather + basin properties (no gauge), scored on the 12 only

unseen50_w_static.label: one LSTM trained on the 50 other rivers, past weather + basin properties: the 12 are rivers never seen

unseen50_w_nostatic.label: one LSTM trained on the 50 other rivers, past weather only (no basin properties): the 12 are rivers never seen

lstm63eq_wq.label: as lstm63_wq with 5x the update limit (10000) and 5x the patience window (a check every 500 updates, stop after 6 without gain)

notes: Quoting. The sentence in `outcome` is accurate arithmetic but incomplete as a statement of the result: any document (report, README, slides, Q&A, guide) must quote `outcome_full` (the outcome plus `outcome_caveat`), never `outcome` alone. Both are computed from the tables of this file.

Design (a). lstm63_wq and lstm63_w are one LSTM each, trained on the 63 south-eastern CAMELS basins with a complete record (the 12 study basins and the 51 others of results/basin_audit.csv; flood.candidate_ids(), checked when loaded: a row for every day of 1980-10-01 to 2014-09-30, no missing value, all ten properties present: data_checks). Network, inputs, settings (results/lstm_all.json, key config) and seeds are those of the stored controls lstm_wq and lstm_w; the only change is the list of training rivers. Scalers (weather, flow, the ten properties) and loss weights come from the training years of the training rivers. The networks are scored on the 12 only and the saved prediction sets hold the 12 (flood.evaluate, the same thresholds, the same test years as every set of the report); the 12 inside the 63-basin tables are bit-identical to the stored 12-basin tables (data_checks).

Stopping. flood.fit is unchanged: at every check it scores the validation years (2000-2005) of ALL its training rivers and stops on their mean NSE over rivers and leads. With 63 rivers that mean includes the 12, so the stopping point is chosen on the validation years of 63 rivers, not of the 12 (and of the 50, never the 12, for the never-seen models). stopping.*.validation_nse_of_the_12_at_that_update gives the 12's own validation score at the chosen update, information only: nothing was chosen on it; for the stored 12-river controls it equals the trainer's own best_val_nse (checked).

Training per river. Each update draws 32 sequences of one river each, uniformly over the training rivers, so with 63 rivers a river gets about a fifth of the sequences per update. The 12-river controls ran 1233 updates on average (best at 633): 1689 sequences per river at the best update; the 63-river models ran 1700 (best at 1100): 559 sequences per river, 0.33 times the control's. 0 of 5 lstm63_wq trainings and 0 of 5 lstm63_w trainings reached the update limit of 2000 before the stopping rule was met (controls: 0 of 3 and 0 of 3). lstm63eq_wq is the arm with five times the update limit (10000) and the patience window (a check every 500 updates, the same patience of 6 checks): it ran 4100 updates on average, but its kept networks are at 1500, 1000, 1000, 1000, 1000 updates (mean 1100; 559 sequences per river against 1689 for the 12-river controls), where those of lstm63_wq are (mean 1100): seed 0: 0.372 at 1500 updates, 0.326 at the last check (4500); seed 1: 0.377 at 1000 updates, 0.319 at the last check (4000); seed 2: 0.378 at 1000 updates, 0.346 at the last check (4000); seed 3: 0.378 at 1000 updates, 0.286 at the last check (4000); seed 4: 0.377 at 1000 updates, 0.339 at the last check (4000). A longer patience window did not move the optimum; it is not equal training per river, which would need about 3300 updates (63 x 1689 / 32), fixed rather than early-stopped (stopping.updates_for_equal_sequences_per_river_at_63_rivers).

Design (b). unseen50_w_static and unseen50_w_nostatic: past weather only (a river without a gauge has no flow input), trained on the 50 other rivers - the 51 minus 03471500, which lies inside 03473000 (S F Holston River near Damascus): the outlines show 198 km2, 100% of 03471500 and 25% of 03473000's basin, so for that river the 51-river design would not be a river never seen; no other pair of the 12 x 12 and 12 x 51 outlines shares any area (0 others found). Scalers, loss weights and the stopping point come from the 50 rivers only (the validation years of the 50); one model forecasts all 12; the high-flow level of each of the 12 (observed 95th percentile of its training years) is used for scoring only, as in 05_lobo.py. The 12's flow is never read in training (leak_probes.training_ignores_the_12). Same settings as lstm_w, five seeds per variant (05_lobo.py had one training per river).

Comparability with 05_lobo.py is limited, in this order. (1) Proximity and the rest of the design: the nearest training gauge is a median of 39.3 km from the 12 here and 110.1 km in the leave-one-out test (8 against 4 of the 12 have a training gauge within 50 km); the nearest training basin in the ten-property space the model sees is 1.42 against 2.23 (5 against 7 of the 12 have a property outside the training range). Neighbouring rivers share storms and geology, so 'never seen' here means 'no flow record of this river', not 'far from any gauged river'. The number of training rivers, their variety and their nearness to the 12 change together between the two designs and were not separated: the gain over the 05 models does not rank with the distance to the nearest of the 50 training gauges (Spearman rho -0.18, p = 0.572 with properties; -0.31, p = 0.331 without; 12 rivers), and the 5 rivers whose nearest training gauge is no closer with the 50 gained a median of +0.149 and +0.096; the independent review (round 1, on the networks of seeds 0-2 and their three-seed averages) also scored the saved 50-river networks on the 12 and on 15 further never-seen rivers whose flow record has gaps (n = 27) and found that their NSE does not fall with the distance to the nearest training gauge (Spearman rho +0.09, p = 0.669 with properties; +0.24, p = 0.238 without; results/review_more_basins.json). A buffered leave-out (train on the 50 minus every river within 50 and 100 km of the one held out) or a dose-response over random subsets of 11, 25 and 50 rivers would separate them; neither was done. (2) One model scores all 12 here against twelve different models in 05, so the seed noise is shared by all 12 scores and the 12 scores are not independent draws. (3) The 50 are 22 northern lowland, 18 southern lowland and 10 mountain basins (the 11 of 05 were four per landscape less the one held out); Hyco Creek, NC and Myakka, FL have a larger share of days without any flow (5.2% and 0.6%) than any of the 50 (largest 0.4%), so they are rivers of a kind the 50 do not hold. (4) Budget and stopping: 05 capped its trainings at 1000 updates and patience 4, one seed; here 2000 / 6, five seeds. (5) Single trainings against seed averages: the 05 numbers are single trainings, and the five-seed average of unseen50_w_static is 0.031 above the mean of its single trainings (0.017 for unseen50_w_nostatic), so unseen.against_the_leave_one_out_models.<pair>.<lead>.single_trainings (each single 50-river training against the 05 number, with its Wilcoxon p) is the like-for-like comparison. round_1.verdict: The numbers, the data, the engine change and the saved networks of E3 hold up under independent recomputation; I found no leakage and no arithmetic error. Every headline number of results/more_basins.json (five new sets, seven controls, three leads, and the 20 seed and average files) was reproduced with my own code to 0.0, also by flood.evaluate; the seed averages are bitwise means of their seed files, obs are the project's flow bit for bit, the stored sets hold exactly the 12. The engine change is confined to basins() and load_data(): with no ids the hand-in engine and the present engine rebuild the same 9,543,479-byte cache from the raw files, equal to the stored one; thresholds and the lstm_wq headline (median NSE 0.5896, 18.66% of onsets) are unchanged; no other script passes ids; test_flood.py passes and its new check fails for all eight deliberately broken load_data() variants. The 63 basins are exactly what the audit rule gives (recomputed from the raw files for all 78 candidates), their cache equals tables I rebuilt bit for bit, and the 12 inside it equal the stored 12. All 15 saved networks reproduce their stored forecasts bit for bit from the file alone (also with my own input matrix); their scalers equal my recomputation from the training years of the training rivers; early stopping used the validation years of the 63 (of the 50, never the 12, for the never-seen models). The never-seen training never reads the 12 (fit with the 12 absent from the dictionary gives identical weights); the nested gauge 03471500 lies 100% inside 03473000 and is the only overlapping pair of the 63. The interim scoring pass did not influence the equal-training arm: the 15-training plan is the first line of the log, the killed run printed the arm's curve and the rerun the same numbers, and the other four sets' results are unchanged. The gain rule, its words and all verdicts reproduce exactly. What the experiment shows is smaller than its sentences, and three statements say more than the data. (1) With the gauge, 63 rivers give no clear NSE gain at 1 day (0.590 -> 0.604, inside the 12-river seed range), a clear one at 2 and 3 days (+0.022, +0.028) and much steadier trainings; the onsets are not 'a clear loss': at the fixed level the model warns of 8 fewer onsets and 59 fewer false alarms with the same CSI (McNemar p = 0.24), at the level chosen on validation it warns of more (21.6% against 18.7%); the verdict stays NOT YET (must-fix 1). (2) The 'equal training' arm is not equal at the kept network: its checkpoints are the same early ones as the 1x arm (593 sequences per river against 1689 for the control), because the 63-river validation score peaks at 1000-1500 updates; it shows that a longer patience window does not move the optimum. (3) For rivers never seen, 50 training rivers give +0.16 (with properties) and +0.12 (weather only) NSE over the 05 numbers in every seed, and that survives the seed-average and budget differences; but it compares a three-seed average of one model with single trainings (a single seed's p is 0.05-0.09 with properties), and it cannot be attributed to the number of rivers: it does not rank with the distance to the nearest training gauge (rho -0.36, p 0.26) and the 50-river networks do not score lower on 27 never-seen rivers the farther they lie (rho +0.09), yet the two designs differ in number, variety and neighbours at once; the test that would separate scale from proximity (buffered leave-out, dose-response) needs training and was not done. Open before E3 can enter the report: must-fix 1 and 2 and the wording items of should-fix 1 to 5; the outcome sentence is fair arithmetic but must not be quoted without a corrected outcome_caveat.
